newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's PSL party pressures PM over farm policy.
newsitem.headline: Poland's PSL party pressures PM over farm policy.

text.p: Poland's Peasant Party (PSL), part of the ruling coalition, turned up the heat on Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz on Monday in a bid to force him to grant its farm policy demands just a month before general elections.
The PSL drafted a no-confidence motion against former communist Cimoszewicz, though a senior official said the party might still drop it if the cabinet met its demands.

"We have collected enough signatures under our motion to hold a parliamentary no-confidence vote against the prime minister," Janusz Piechocinski, a deputy head of the PSL parliamentary caucus, told Reuters.

The Peasant Party is demanding the government grants advance payments to farmers for this year's harvest, arguing that this will help them through a difficult period following last month's flooding, and help stabilise grain prices after the harvest.
The PSL said last week it would propose a no-confidence vote against Cimoszewicz, a member of the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), accusing him of a delay in giving farmers advances.
Finance Minister Marek Belka said the advances were too costly for the state budget.
Piechocinski made clear, however, that the PSL could abandon the no-confidence motion if the cabinet approved the proposals at its session on Tuesday.
"For us, personal changes are not the most important issue...it is important that the right farm policies are implemented," he said.
Government spokeswoman Aleksandra Jakubowska told a news briefing the advance payments for farmers were on the government's agenda for Tuesday.
President Aleksander Kwasniewski, linked to the ex-communist party, dismissed the Peasants' actions as campaigning before the September 21 elections.
Opinion polls show the PSL's rating in decline, with the party badly trailing the election favourites -- the opposition Solidarity Election Action and the SLD.

The no-confidence motion, which could be voted on in late August, has little chance of success because the opposition is opposed to it and the PSL does not have the simple majority required to push it through.
